name: Diamond Push-Up
description: The diamond push-up is a push-up variation where the thumbs and index fingers touch to form a diamond or triangle shape beneath the chest. This narrow hand position dramatically increases triceps brachii activation while the pectoralis major acts as a secondary mover. It is one of the most effective bodyweight exercises for tricep development.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a standard push-up position, then bring both hands together under the sternum with the thumbs and forefingers touching to form a diamond shape. Arms should be fully extended.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment needed. Find a flat, stable surface for the hands.
steps: Step 1: Position hands together on the floor below the chest with thumbs and index fingers touching to form a diamond shape.
Step 2: Extend arms fully; keep the body in a rigid plank from head to heels.
Step 3: Inhale and lower the chest toward the diamond by bending the elbows, which will move outward slightly to either side.
Step 4: Lower until the chest nearly touches the hands, pause briefly, then exhale and press back to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on the descent; exhale on the press.
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows wide, which shifts load away from the triceps
Letting the hips drop or rise out of a neutral plank position
safety_considerations: If wrist discomfort occurs, slightly rotate hands outward a few degrees
Reduce range of motion if shoulder impingement is felt
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Lower the chest to touch or nearly touch the hands, then press fully back to extension.
coaching_cues: Think 'elbows back' as you descend to maximize tricep engagement
Keep the torso rigid — imagine a straight rod from crown to heel
